This medication should not be used during pregnancy as it may harm the fetus. 3. This medication can pass into breast milk and may reduce both the quality and quantity of milk produced. 4. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. 5. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. Keep a detailed list of all products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. 6. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, potentially causing false results. Inform your healthcare provider and laboratory personnel if you are using this medication. 7. If someone overdoses on this medication and experiences severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. 8. Regular physical exams, including laboratory and medical tests (e.g., blood pressure checks, breast exams/mammograms, pelvic exams, Pap smears), should be conducted while using this medication. Follow your doctor’s instructions for self-examining your breasts and report any lumps immediately. 9. Preventing or managing high blood pressure, high cholesterol, and diabetes can reduce your risk of heart disease and stroke. Lifestyle changes such as reducing stress, eating a low-fat/low-salt diet, losing weight if overweight, exercising regularly, and quitting smoking can help control or prevent these conditions. 10. Engage in mental exercises, such as reading or solving crossword puzzles, to help prevent dementia. 11. Store this medication at room temperature. Do not remove the ring from its pouch until ready for use. 12. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. 13. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. 14. This medication is a hormone (estrogen) used by women to reduce symptoms of menopause, such as hot flashes and vaginal dryness, which occur due to decreased estrogen production in the body. 15. Before using this medication, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Wash and dry your hands before handling the ring. Insert the ring high into the vagina as directed. 16. The ring is typically left in place for three months, after which it should be removed and replaced with a new ring if treatment is to continue. Do not leave the ring in place for longer than three months. 17. If the ring is inserted properly, you should not feel it, and it should not interfere with sexual intercourse. If you feel the ring or experience slight discomfort, it may not be positioned high enough. 18. If the ring falls out of the vagina, rinse it with lukewarm water and reinsert it. 19. To remove the ring, hook your finger through it and gently pull it out. Contact your doctor if you have difficulty removing the ring. Discard the used ring in the trash. 20. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, bloating, breast tenderness, headache, or weight changes. 21. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. 22. Rarely, this medication may cause serious, sometimes fatal, problems due to blood clots, such as heart attack, stroke, or clots in the lungs or legs. 23. Vaginal rings have rarely been associated with a very serious, potentially fatal bacterial infection known as toxic shock syndrome (TSS). 24. Severe allergic reactions to this product are rare. 25. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. 26. Before using estradiol, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. 27. Do not smoke or use tobacco while on this medication. 28. Inform your doctor if you have recently had or will be undergoing surgery, or if you will be confined to a chair or bed for an extended period (e.g., during a long plane flight), as these conditions increase the risk of blood clots, especially when using an estrogen product. 29. This medication may cause blotchy, dark areas on your face and skin (melasma). Sunlight may worsen this effect. Limit your time in the sun and avoid tanning booths and sunlamps. 30. If you are nearsighted or wear contact lenses, you may develop vision problems or difficulty wearing your lenses. 31. If you develop a vaginal infection while using this ring, you may leave the ring in place while treating the infection, unless otherwise directed by your doctor. 32. This medication should not be used during pregnancy. 33. This medication passes into breast milk and may reduce the quality and quantity of milk produced.
